annotation.method: Codex freshly reread the complete 16-page local paper, rechecked Model 1 and the full derivations of Theorems 3.1 and 4.1, compared candidates with the frozen Mathlib and NumStability baselines, rejected the coefficient-mismatched T1 formulation, and retained only the source-faithful T3 target.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P20 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

rejected_candidates.reason: These define the hardware and arithmetic hypotheses rather than a selected conclusion; the frozen library already contains a broader additive-underflow witness hierarchy.

The displayed relation uses an asymptotic less-similar sign after dropping terms and would require additional executable scaling and underflow semantics. The former no-underflow T1 was also removed because it changed the paper's nU coefficient to gamma_n(U).

rejected_candidates.candidate: equation (3.13), the scaled input-conversion error bound
rejected_candidates.reason: Rejected for T1: the nearby NumStability theorem packages matrix-product expansion and triangle-inequality composition that the N condition can reconstruct quickly from Mathlib, so it does not make the L condition substantially faster.

rejected_candidates.candidate: equation (3.16), the bound for one accumulation-underflow error
rejected_candidates.reason: This is an exact valid source result, but the concrete frozen-library check found that its proof reduces to the two inverse-scale inequalities and scalar arithmetic. It therefore does not materially combine multiple NumStability results and would be T1 rather than the required T2 slot.

rejected_candidates.candidate: the post-(3.26) comparison of accumulation- and input-underflow terms
rejected_candidates.reason: Under literal Model 1, format nesting does not imply Gmin <= gmin when the two formats use different subnormal modes. Adding that comparison as a hypothesis makes the formal target weaker than the written claim, so the audited task was rejected.

This induction is supporting machinery rather than the selected conclusion. Its decomposition consequences and the pre-theorem estimates through (4.27) are represented by the fixed Section 4 derivation used by T3, whose target is Theorem 4.1.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Figures 5.1-5.2 and the large-n divergence discussion
rejected_candidates.reason: These are finite experiments and empirical observations, not universally quantified mathematical conclusions.

rejected_candidates.candidate: generalization to other linear algebra computations in Section 6
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper presents this as an expectation contingent on finding suitable scaling, not a proved result.

T1.decision: Skipped after strict source audit: equations (3.21) and (3.23) use the paper's coefficient ((2u+u^2)(1+nU)+nU). The discarded target replaced nU with gamma_n(U) and therefore stated a different exact theorem. The exact paper coefficient is not supplied by the available NumStability matrix-product theorem.

T2.decision: Skipped: no source candidate needs two independent substantial mounted NumStability results.

T3.decision: Use Theorem 4.1's fixed round-to-nearest scaled p-word computation and its normwise forward-error bound; NumStability has no corresponding multiword narrow-range theorem.

selection_policy: Represent an undefined first-order lesssim by an explicit second-order remainder instead of silently replacing it with an exact displayed inequality.
Represent input and accumulation underflow contributions separately.
Do not promote experimental curves, qualified expectations, or future generalizations to theorem targets.
Keep every public definition free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only after comparison with the complete frozen NumStability source and the compiled condition-L bundle recorded in metadata/library_olean.json.
